John Levy is one of the few figures in jazz who has employed his musical prowess as a performer and a businessman. He was born in New Orleans on March 4, 1912 but grew up in Chicago when jazz was king. His boyhood friends included Milt Hinton and Ray Nance and he took up the violin at age eight, later moving to the bass. Early gigs included work with Earl Hines and Stuff Smith, who brought him to New York in 1943. He gained more experience with Don Byas, Errol Garner and Ben Webster, eventually becoming a member of the soon-to-be-famous George Shearing Quintet. John showed a talent for organization and eventually put performing aside to become Shearing’s personal manager. His success in this field attracted other clients including Joe Williams and Nancy Wilson. Today John still acts as their manager and was recently presented with a gift of a new bass by his famous clients.
Mr. Levy was interviewed in the Caribbean aboard a cruise ship on May 31, 1995 by Monk Rowe.

We are here today filming for the Hamilton Jazz Archive and we’re going to get a little different slant today. We’ve been talking to a lot of musicians about their experiences in the jazz world in association with Count Basie and Joe Williams. Today we have John Levy with us, who is a longtime friend, associate and manager with Joe Williams and we’re going to talk a little bit about how he looks at the music business. The business of music is something that sometimes musicians don’t deal with as much as they should perhaps. And I would have to tell you that yesterday we had a long conversation between Milt Hinton and Joe Williams and they spoke very highly of you, and so I’d have to say you’re doing something right over all these years.
